title: Processes: O11 BPT processes (process, start/end, automatic and human activities, connectors) proven by jobs; ODC workflows are not module-model elements on any public route

capabilities.title: BPT process: process, start/end, automatic and human activities, connectors, edit and delete an activity
capabilities.summary: IProcess under the module (inputs as IInputParameter, Detail expression); inside it IStartNode, IAutomaticActivityNode (with its own action flow), IHumanActivityNode (Label, Destination = a screen, arguments by name, Instructions, DueDate, AllowSkip) and IEndNode, joined with link {from, to}; layout {target} arranges the canvas. An activity with a consumer (its incoming connector) is deleted only after the consumer is removed.

route.operation: create IProcess @espace; create IStartNode/IAutomaticActivityNode/IHumanActivityNode/IEndNode under the process; link {from,to}; layout {target}; set Detail / Label / Destination / Instructions / DueDate / AllowSkip; deliver with o11_deliver (it validates and refuses before any change)

capabilities.guidance: Addressing outside the creating job: IProcess:<Process> and activities by path IProcess:<Process>/<Activity>; connectors by #IActionConnector under their source. The body of an automatic activity is logic (front A): nodes inside the activity ($auto/#IStartNode ... #IEndNode). A human activity's Destination is a screen (front B) and its arguments are set by name ($human/<Input> Value). A minimal process without a Taskbox detail screen raises ProcessMissingInboxDetail (declared in process-bpt).

read.route: get/dump IProcess:<Process> (depth 2-3 shows activities and connectors)

preconditions: the consumer of an activity is its incoming connector

o11.scope: the connector from Start before and after it is removed

preconditions: create Start, the activities and End, then link them in order
a process without a Taskbox detail screen raises ProcessMissingInboxDetail

o11.scope: including an activity added between two existing nodes of a process another job created, with its own action flow

set.route: set {target, prop, value}; link {from, to} for connectors

o11.scope: Detail (an expression over the process inputs)
Label, Destination (a screen), arguments by name, Instructions, DueDate, AllowSkip

preconditions: an activity with a consumer (incoming connector) is refused: remove the connector first (delete <source>/#IActionConnector), then delete the activity and relink

o11.scope: deleted after its incoming connector was removed; the process stays valid (Start -> NotifyOwner -> End)

limits.text: Wait, conditional start, decision, execute-process, send-email (process) nodes, activity output parameters and process callbacks have factories in the API but no job: they are undetermined on this lane, not proven.
The refusal of deleting an activity that still has a consumer is not in a negative job: the job description says it was pasted in a report outside the repository, so its text is not verified here.

differences.text: ODC has no proven route for processes/workflows: IESpace.CreateProcess and CreateBusinessProcess exist in the ODC API and were never measured, and ODC workflows are a separate asset type (see process.odc-workflow).
differences.origin: kernel/docs/NAO-DA.md:371-392 (BPT / CreateBusinessProcess, REFUTADO, creation in a module not measured)

unavailable.reason: No proven route on ODC: processes are Workflows, a separate asset type (SegmentationKind.BusinessProcess) written in the ODC Portal Workflow Editor, which the ODC Studio refuses to open; IESpace.CreateBusinessProcess and CreateProcess exist in the ODC Model API but creating either inside a module was never measured; no job or feature creates them.
unavailable.evidence: kernel/docs/NAO-DA.md:371-392 (BPT / IESpace.CreateBusinessProcess, REFUTADO: the feature exists as a Workflow asset; creation in a module not measured); no job in kernel/tests/jobs-odc or jobs-odc-negative (declared, not executed)
unavailable.alternative: none in the module model; a workflow is a Portal asset (outside this catalog). Server-side scheduling inside the module: timer.schedule
